subject: optical fiber cable
title: A Glass Thread as Thin as a Hair Outran Japan's Whole Internet

scenes.text: A glass thread as thin as a hair outran Japan's internet.
In 2025, Japanese engineers pushed over a million gigabits a second through one single fiber.
That's about twenty-six times the download traffic of every home connection in Japan combined.
And they kept it up over eighteen hundred kilometres, about Berlin to Naples.
The trick: inside that one strand run nineteen separate cores, each carrying its own light.
Yet it's exactly as thick as the fibers already buried under city streets. Just nineteen times the lanes.

description:
One optical fiber, just 0.125 millimetres thick, carried more data than Japan's entire home internet.
In 2025 Japan's NICT and partners sent 1.02 petabits per second over 1,808 kilometres through a 19-core fiber with the same standard cladding diameter as ordinary single-core fiber. That is about 26 times the total download traffic of Japan's fixed broadband subscribers, and over 3.5 million times faster than a typical US home connection.
What would you download first at that speed?
first_comment: The record is about 3.5 million times faster than an average US home connection. Would you rather have that speed at home, or unlimited battery on your phone?
